instruction: I have file1.xlsx and file2.ods on my Desktop. Using only the command line, count the total number of data rows (excluding headers) in both files combined, and save the count to ~/Desktop/total_count.txt

metadata.explanation: Task requires counting total data rows from both files using command line. Verified with Python: file1.xlsx has 5000 data rows (excluding header), file2.ods has 5000 data rows, total is 10000. The output text file should contain '10000'. Evaluator checks the text content matches '10000'.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the output file at /home/user/Desktop/total_count.txt using env.controller.get_file()
Getter properly handles file content by decoding UTF-8 and stripping whitespace
Metric correctly performs exact string comparison between result and expected value
Expected value '10000' is semantically correct (verified: 5000 + 5000 = 10000 total data rows)
Evaluator logic correctly handles expected parameter when type='rule' (receives '10000' directly from get_rule())
Whitespace handling is robust: both getter and metric strip whitespace to handle trailing newlines
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies the exact requirement (count saved to file)
Data flow is logically correct: file content extraction -> string comparison -> pass/fail
